answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small deposit and pass a live, randomized proof-of-work check before joining, like a jetty that admits only one boat at a time. Reputation should then grow slowly, like a willow adding rings, so a fresh fake cannot instantly borrow trust. Finally, route attestations through a prism of independent checks — stake history, work quality, and peer diversity — so no single signal can be gamed, and a cluster of identical newcomers stands out at once.
